author: Rudy Blalock
title: ICE Seeks Hold on New York Rape Suspect; State Ignored 16,000 Detainers Since January 2025, DHS Says
text:
Federal immigration officials have asked New York City authorities to hold a man accused of raping a 28-year-old woman, as the Department of Homeland Security says authorities across the state have ignored more than 16,000 immigration detainers since January 2025.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement lodged the request for Reynaldo Hoel Mayna, a Peruvian citizen, on Nov. 3 after his arrest by New York City police, the department said Thursday. State authorities did not honor 16,070 detainers between Jan. 20, 2025, and Oct. 8, 2026—a period that covers more than 20 months—according to ICE figures cited in the statement.
Mayna entered the country illegally near San Diego and was arrested by Border Patrol agents on Aug. 18, 2023. He was later released into the United States during the Biden administration.

“Sanctuary politicians have handcuffed their law enforcement and are allowing criminal activity to thrive, while the American people become less safe,” Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.
NTD News contacted the NYPD for details about the alleged attack and clarification on Mayna’s charges and criminal history but did not immediately receive a response.
Across New York, the unhonored detainers were linked to 52,503 criminal charges and convictions. The department combined those two categories rather than reporting them separately.
The totals included 131 homicide offenses, 132 kidnappings, 1,017 sexual offenses and 9,502 assaults. The figures also included drug, weapons, robbery, burglary and impaired-driving offenses.
The department pointed to actions by Gov. Kathy Hochul and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as part of its criticism of local limits on immigration enforcement.

The Local Cops, Local Crimes Act, signed May 27, barred agreements that allow local officers to carry out federal civil immigration enforcement duties and gave agencies until Aug. 25 to end them. The lawsuit seeks a court order forcing the sheriff’s office to end its agreement and declaring it invalid under state law.

The order bars city agencies from sharing residents’ information with federal immigration authorities unless required by law and requires a judge’s warrant for federal authorities to enter city property, including schools, shelters and hospitals.
DHS cited several other cases to support its criticism, including a detainer filed in March for Bairon Posada-Hernandez, a Honduran man accused of pushing two people onto subway tracks.
One victim, 83-year-old Air Force veteran Richard Williams, later died from his injuries.
